title: The Sediment Chamber Where Channels Rest

features.name: the layered channels
features.desc-on-touch: Sediment upon sediment: each band holds a different version of how the signal moved. The oldest rests at the bottom; the newest is still settling into place. You can read the history by colour, by grain.

features.name: the comparison seam
features.desc-on-touch: Where two distinct layers meet—one flow stops, another begins. The archive reads differences in the grain, in the pause, in the boundary between what was and what became.

features.name: the fossilized relay
features.desc-on-touch: A node-arm, or a root, preserved in stone—proof that the mesh grew through this ground once, and the stone remembered. The landscape itself became archive.

features.name: the compaction weight
features.desc-on-touch: All the messages above pressing down on all the channels below. Pressure has a grammar here—each layer speaks to the ones beneath it, and is spoken to by the ones above.

features.name: the reading edge
features.desc-on-touch: Where the ground cuts open—a cliff face where each layer is visible at once, all channels exposed to air simultaneously. The archive reads itself as if geology were text.

inscription: in these strata every channel has become history; comparison is just geology reading itself
